4001.sigma:
title: Curl SOCKS5 Hostname Resolution Invocation (CVE-2023-38545 Trigger Path)
id: 6d3a7a1c-4a3b-4f7e-9b2a-9a1e9f5c2c11
description: Detects curl invocations using SOCKS5 with remote hostname resolution, the precondition required to trigger the CVE-2023-38545 heap buffer overflow in libcurl 7.69.0 - 8.3.0.
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/curl-high-severity-vulnerability-oct-2023/
  - https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2023-38545.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/23
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1203
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '/curl'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--socks5-hostname'
      - 'socks5h://'
      - '-x socks5h'
      - '--proxy socks5h'
  condition: selection_img and selection_cmd
level: medium
4001.spl: | tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="curl.exe" OR Processes.process_name="curl") AND (Processes.process="*--socks5-hostname*" OR Processes.process="*socks5h://*" OR Processes.process="*-x socks5h*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
4001.datadog: source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security OR linux.auditd) (@Image:(*\\curl.exe OR *\\Curl.exe OR *\\CURL.EXE) OR @process.executable.path:(*/curl OR */bin/curl OR */usr/bin/curl)) (@CommandLine:(*--socks5-hostname* OR *socks5h\:\/\/* OR *"-x socks5h"*) OR @process.command_line:(*--socks5-hostname* OR *socks5h\:\/\/* OR *"-x socks5h"*))
4001.falcon:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\curl\.exe$/i OR ImageFileName=/\/curl$/i
| regex("(--socks5-hostname|socks5h:\/\/|-x\s+socks5h|--proxy\s+socks5h)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())

id: 7d3a0f6e-1c5a-4e91-9c2c-1f3b8c2b5f10
status: experimental
description: Detects execution of the macOS `defaults` CLI reading NSUserDictionaryReplacementItems, the global preference holding keyboard text replacements. Developers commonly bind sensitive snippets (passwords, SSH keys, credit-card numbers) to these macros, and the read can be triggered by any non-privileged process — including a malicious npm postinstall hook.
references:
    - https://snyk.io/blog/using-insecure-npm-package-manager-defaults/
    - https://www.yagiz.co/using-insecure-npm-defaults/
